chapter: Decca years and the First Herd
title: Rehearsing with Stravinsky at the Paramount Theatre
summary: The band dressed up to rehearse with Stravinsky between shows at the Paramount; he rehearsed in a sweatshirt and towel and was unaware they were doing shows.

story.theme_name: Band pranks, jokes and gigs gone wrong
story.community_name: Pranks, practical jokes and band humor

blocks.x: Okay. Didn't you tell me some anecdotal things about how the band was playing flying somewhere, and they were rehearsing and they I'd have had to come back downstairs --
Oh, yeah, that was with Mr. Stravinsky. We rehearsed --he arrived while we were doing an engagement at the Paramount Theatre.

And it was a long engagement, I think eight or ten weeks. And I don't know just when this transpired, except on his arrival, the whole band hurried after the first show to get to this rehearsal hall on the top floor, but everyone stopped in the dressing rooms to change clothes and put on a dark blue suit and shirt and tie and things that are not normal with musicians, because it was such a great honor that this man had come.
So Stravinsky arrived, wearing a sweatshirt and a pair of slacks and a towel around his neck. He was ready to go to work. And so we rehearsed for about an hour, an hour

and a half, as long well as we could. And then the buzzer buzzed, and he was really having a marvelous time, and telling me what a lovely family I had and how pleased he was that the music sounded as good as it did and so on.

And then he would go downstairs to -- someone would escort him downstairs to go to Sardi's, which was next door and have a little something, a little vodka and a little something there, a little champagne. Then they would say, 'Okav, we go back to rehearsal.' So he'd come back up, and we had just come out of the pit and did another show.

Well, this went on all day and all night. Finally, by the second day, someone got over the fact that -- no one wanted to really mention it -- the fact that we could only stay so long, we had to come back and so on, because we were doing shows. He said, 'Oh, you're doing shows? That's lovely.' So he came down and finally watched our stage show, this was the third day.
Yeah, it's pretty amusing, but we were slowly going under from lack of energy.

But those were exciting times, and just as there will always be exciting times for anyone who's in a position to be experimenting and doing new things, with new music and so on. That's the lifeblood of the whole thing.
